card: Try-ons, fit checks, outfit photos, and review-style clips from one garment photo.

faq.q: Can one garment photo make both a vertical clip and a listing image?
faq.a: Yes. Use a tall 9:16 video at 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for a turn or a short walk. The same photo can also make a still of someone wearing it. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. A still image is 24 credits.

faq.q: Can a flat-lay photo become a photo of someone wearing the piece?
faq.a: Yes. Smooth the garment, shoot the whole piece in even light, or paste a product link, and describe the avatar and the room.

faq.q: Will the print or the fabric change?
faq.a: The result follows your photo. Fine stripes, embroidery, and buttons stay closer when the upload is sharp. If a trim moves, make another version. A failed job returns its credits.

faq.q: Can I show a plus-size or petite build?
faq.a: Yes. Describe height, build, and age range in plain words. The AI avatar is generated for the ad.

faq.q: What photo works when someone should appear in the clothes?
faq.a: Lay it flat or hang it, with the whole garment visible, front side up, in even light. The outline, color, print, and fastenings all need to be clear.

faq.q: How do I keep the fabric color accurate?
faq.a: Shoot in soft daylight, not under a warm lamp, and name the color in plain words.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid clothing ads?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in paid ads. Size and fabric details have to match the real item.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a creator?
faq.a: You pick an AI avatar and pay the credits shown before the job, not a creator fee. Post the clip as an ad.

faq.q: Can a try-on include a voice and captions?
faq.a: Yes. The clip can include a spoken line and captions, and you can publish it to TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook.
